proofs.full_local_argument: Let F_{k-1}=sigma(xi_1,...,xi_{k-1}), g_k=gradient f(x_k), and delta_k=G(x_k,xi_k)-g_k. Measurability, independence and the pointwise moment assumptions imply E[delta_k|F_{k-1}]=0 and E[||delta_k||^2|F_{k-1}]<=sigma^2. All required expectations are finite: x1 is deterministic; ||gradient f(x)||<=||gradient f(x1)||+L||x-x1|| and E||G(x_k,xi_k)||^2<=2 E||gradient f(x_k)||^2+2 sigma^2 inductively give finite second moments of x_k and g_k for every finite k. The smoothness bound about x1 gives integrability of f(x_k). To justify the descent inequality directly, for d=y-x integrate gradient f(x+t d) along t in [0,1]; the difference from <gradient f(x),d> is at most integral_0^1 Lt||d||^2 dt=L||d||^2/2. Apply this to d=-gamma_k(g_k+delta_k). Expanding gives f(x_{k+1})<=f(x_k)-(gamma_k-L gamma_k^2/2)||g_k||^2-(gamma_k-L gamma_k^2)<g_k,delta_k>+(L gamma_k^2/2)||delta_k||^2. Conditional expectation eliminates the cross term, so (gamma_k-L gamma_k^2/2)E||g_k||^2<=E f(x_k)-E f(x_{k+1})+(L sigma^2 gamma_k^2/2). Sum k=1,...,N and use f(x_{N+1})>=f*: sum_k w_k E||g_k||^2<=2 Delta+L sigma^2 sum_k gamma_k^2. Since S>0 and R is independent of the full trajectory, E||gradient f(x_R)||^2=sum_k (w_k/S)E||g_k||^2. Division proves the equivalent unscaled bound, and D_f^2=2 Delta/L gives the source normalization. For the stopped implementation couple it to this full sample sequence and the same R; its iterates through x_R coincide, so its output has the same law.

assumptions: f:R^n->R is differentiable, bounded below, and ||gradient f(x)-gradient f(y)||<=L||x-y|| for all x,y. x1 is deterministic. Convexity and attainment of f* are not required.

For each k, xi_k is fresh and independent of xi_1,...,xi_{k-1} and R. G is Borel measurable. For every deterministic x and each k, E G(x,xi_k)=gradient f(x) and E||G(x,xi_k)-gradient f(x)||^2<=sigma^2.
The steps are deterministic and satisfy 0<gamma_k<2/L for every k=1,...,N.
statement.conclusion: (1/L) E||gradient f(x_R)||^2 <= (D_f^2+sigma^2 sum_{k=1}^N gamma_k^2)/S. Equivalently E||gradient f(x_R)||^2 <= [2 Delta+L sigma^2 sum_{k=1}^N gamma_k^2]/[sum_{k=1}^N(2 gamma_k-L gamma_k^2)].
statement.objects_and_definitions: Use the Euclidean norm on R^n. Let f*=inf_{x in R^n} f(x), Delta=f(x1)-f*, D_f=sqrt(2 Delta/L). Define the full trajectory x_{k+1}=x_k-gamma_k G(x_k,xi_k), k=1,...,N. Set w_k=2 gamma_k-L gamma_k^2, S=sum_k w_k, and independently draw R with P(R=k)=w_k/S. The stopped implementation has the same output law.
statement.parameter_domains: n,N are positive integers; L>0; finite sigma>=0; finite Delta>=0; gamma_k in (0,2/L). Thus all w_k and S are positive.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every positive integer n,N, every admissible f,x1, oracle sequence and deterministic step sequence, the conclusion holds. Expectation is over all oracle samples and the independent output draw R.
